registerNotMeasured: This file is a cognate record created for the n() plural conversion, not an nl pass. The register verdict in docs/l10n-workflow.md §7.2 lists nl as informal, but nothing was measured here and there is no detectors/nl.js, so selfcheck must not report a register result for nl. Measuring it belongs to the Tier 1 re-audit.
scopeNote: COGNATE RECORD ONLY — this is not a finished nl pass. It was created because the n() plural conversion needed '_register_::_registers_', whose Dutch value is spelled exactly as the English, and apply.js gate 3 refuses an identical value without a recorded reason. Creating the file opts nl into cognate enforcement (COGNATES_ENFORCED keys on this file existing), so every one of the bundle's identical values had to be justified here at the same time or test:l10n:parity would fail on them. What is recorded below is therefore the identical-value review and nothing else: no register measurement, no detector, no grammatical audit of the ~1050 pre-existing Transifex values. nl remains on the Tier 1 re-audit list. Two entries carry a caveat rather than a clean justification — read them before treating this file as a finished review.

cognates.Audit: English loan, standard in Dutch governance and compliance language; no native equivalent is in use.
cognates.Avatar: International term, unchanged in Dutch; Nextcloud core nl renders it identically.
cognates.AVG / Verwerkingsregister: The en.js key is itself Dutch — it arrived with the AVG merge on development — so there is nothing to translate.
cognates.Bewaartermijn: The en.js key is itself Dutch (AVG merge) and is already the correct Dutch term.
cognates.Code: Same spelling and meaning in Dutch.
cognates.Complex: Same spelling and meaning in Dutch as an adjective.
cognates.Dashboard: Established English loan in Dutch UI language; core nl keeps it untranslated.
cognates.Deadline: Established English loan; the native alternatives read as legalese in a UI.
cognates.Deck: Nextcloud app name. Kept untranslated in every finished locale.
cognates.DSAR: Acronym (Data Subject Access Request), kept untranslated in Dutch privacy practice.
cognates.Excel (.xlsx): Product name plus a file extension; nothing translatable.
cognates.Filters: Same spelling in Dutch, and the Dutch plural is also 'filters'.
cognates.Flows: The app's own feature name, deliberately kept in English in nl, de and da.
cognates.Host *: 'Host' is the Dutch technical term too; the asterisk is a required-field marker.
cognates.IBANs: Banking acronym; Dutch forms the plural the same way.
cognates.Id: The same acronym in the casing the source uses.
cognates.ID:: Acronym plus a colon; nothing translatable.
cognates.in {register}: 'in' is the same preposition in Dutch; the remainder is a placeholder.
cognates.Interval: Same spelling and meaning in Dutch.
cognates.Label: Established loan, standard in Dutch UI language.
cognates.Labels: Same loan; the Dutch plural is also 'labels'.
cognates.Links: Established loan; the Dutch plural is also 'links'.
cognates.Multitenancy: Technical term with no established Dutch equivalent.
cognates.Naam: The en.js key is itself Dutch (AVG merge) and is already correct.
cognates.Object: Dutch uses 'object' for this concept, spelled exactly as the English.
cognates.object: The same Dutch noun, in the lowercase form the source uses.
cognates.Object #{id}: Dutch noun plus a number sign and a placeholder.
cognates.Object A: Dutch noun plus a bare letter label.
cognates.Object B: Dutch noun plus a bare letter label.
cognates.OpenDocument (.ods): Format name plus a file extension; nothing translatable.
cognates.Parallel:: Same spelling in Dutch, plus a colon.
cognates.pgvector ANN sidecar: Component and product name; nothing translatable.
cognates.Rechtsgrond: The en.js key is itself Dutch (AVG merge) and is already the correct term.
cognates.Register / Schema: Both nouns are spelled the same in Dutch; the rest is a separator.
cognates.register(s): Dutch noun 'register'. CAVEAT: the source's '(s)' happens to read correctly here because the Dutch plural is 'registers', unlike the 'schema(s)' entry below.
cognates.Registers: The Dutch plural of 'register' is also 'registers'.
cognates.Schema: Dutch noun 'schema', spelled exactly as the English.
cognates.schema(s): Dutch noun 'schema'. CAVEAT: recorded as deliberate-identical, not as correct — the Dutch plural is "schema's", so the parenthetical should read "schema('s)". Pre-existing; left for the nl re-audit rather than changed here.
cognates.Slug: Technical term kept in English in nl; core lt translates it, core nl does not.
cognates.Type: Same spelling and meaning in Dutch.
cognates.Verantwoording: The en.js key is itself Dutch (AVG merge) and is already correct.
cognates.Webhooks: Same loan; the Dutch plural is also 'webhooks'.
cognates.Workflows: Established loan; the Dutch plural is also 'workflows'.
cognates.{count} widget(s): 'widget' is an established loan; the rest is a placeholder and a parenthetical.
cognates._register_::_registers_: Dutch spells both forms exactly as the English: singular 'register', plural 'registers'. The bundle's own 'Registers' and 'register(s)' keys already carry the same word, so this is the established term rather than a new choice.
cognates._object_::_objects_: Form 0 only: 'object' is the Dutch noun and is spelled as the English singular. The plural form is 'objecten' and differs.
cognates._schema_::_schemas_: Form 0 only: 'schema' is the Dutch noun and is spelled as the English singular. The plural form is "schema's" and differs.
cognates._{count} schema_::_{count} schemas_: Form 0 only: '{count} schema' matches the English because 'schema' is the Dutch noun. The plural form uses "schema's" and differs.
